questions.stem: Brightwater's nightly job loads 40,000 rows into a warehouse table with one INSERT statement per row, and it gets slower every week. What should it do instead?

options.text: Rebuild the table's statistics after every INSERT
Wrap each INSERT in its own explicit transaction
Run the same single-row INSERTs from more parallel sessions
Stage the rows and load them together, for example with one INSERT ... SELECT or with COPY INTO

questions.explanation: Each small INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE writes its own Parquet file, so many row-level changes leave many small files. Staging the data and loading it in one statement, or with COPY INTO for files, avoids that.

questions.stem: A country_code column holds two-letter codes but was declared varchar(8000). What does the performance guidance say?

options.text: Leave it: string length doesn't affect a warehouse
Store the codes as a JSON array instead
Change it to varchar(max) so it never needs changing again
Use the smallest string length that fits the values, such as varchar(2)

questions.explanation: The guidance is to use the smallest string column length that can hold the values, for example varchar(100) rather than varchar(8000) or varchar(max).

questions.stem: Which two statements about statistics in a Fabric Warehouse are true?

options.text: You can create single-column histogram statistics yourself with CREATE STATISTICS
Statistics are only built when a Spark notebook runs
The engine creates and maintains statistics automatically
You can create multi-column statistics with CREATE STATISTICS

questions.explanation: Automatic statistics are created and maintained by the engine. You can also create, update and drop single-column histogram statistics; multi-column statistics can't be created manually.

questions.stem: A dashboard runs the same SELECT against a warehouse many times an hour, and the tables it reads change once a night. Which feature lets the repeat runs return quickly?

options.text: Result set caching, which keeps the query's final result and reuses it until the tables it reads change
A retention policy
Splitting the query into many single-row SELECTs
Turning off automatic statistics

questions.explanation: Result set caching persists the final result set of applicable SELECT queries so later runs can reuse it. A change to the referenced tables invalidates the cache, so results stay consistent.

questions.stem: After the nightly load changes a table, what happens to a cached result for a query that reads it?

options.text: The cache is copied into the table
The old result keeps being returned until someone clears it by hand
The earlier cache isn't used, so the next run reads the new data
The load fails until the cache is dropped

questions.explanation: Result consistency is kept by invalidating cache created before the data changed.
